$comment: The EventStorming notation as data. Adding a type is one entry here; the web app renders it with the named renderer (sticky, area or lane) or with a renderer registered under a new name.

levels.name: Big Picture
levels.description: Explore a whole business line with everyone who knows a part of it. Start with a flood of Domain Events, then sort them into a timeline, mark Hot Spots and find the pivotal moments.

levels.name: Process Modelling
levels.description: Model one process step by step: an Actor, looking at a Read Model, issues a Command; a system accepts it and a Domain Event happens; a Policy reacts with the next Command.

levels.name: Software Design
levels.description: Design the software: which Aggregate accepts each Command, which Domain Events it emits, and where the boundaries between bounded contexts lie.

types.name: Domain Event
types.description: Something that happened in the domain that a domain expert cares about.
types.whenToUse: For every fact on the timeline. It is the backbone of every board: start here.
types.writingRule: Past tense, business language: "Order Placed", not "Place order" or "OrderCreatedEvent".

types.name: Command
types.description: A decision or intention that causes a Domain Event, issued by an Actor or a Policy.
types.whenToUse: Just before the Domain Event it causes.

types.name: Actor
types.description: A person, role or group who takes a decision - usually by issuing a Command.
types.whenToUse: Next to the Command they issue, or the Domain Event they cause.
types.writingRule: A role, not a name: "Customer", "Restaurant manager".

types.name: Policy
types.description: The reaction to a Domain Event: whenever something happens, then do something. Automated or done by a person.
types.whenToUse: Between a Domain Event and the Command it triggers.
types.writingRule: "Whenever X, then Y": "Whenever payment is declined, notify the customer".
examples: Whenever an order is placed, reserve the dishes
Whenever a delivery is late, offer a voucher

types.name: Read Model
types.description: The information an Actor needs to take a decision.
types.whenToUse: Next to the Actor, before the Command they decide to issue.
types.writingRule: What is shown: "Menu with prices and delivery time".

types.name: External System
types.description: A system outside our control that receives Commands or produces Domain Events: a third party, a legacy system, another department's software.
types.whenToUse: Where the process depends on something we do not own.

types.name: Aggregate / Constraint
types.description: The thing that accepts or rejects a Command, enforcing the business rules, and emits the resulting Domain Events.
types.whenToUse: Between a Command and the Domain Events it produces.
types.writingRule: A noun, optionally with its key rules: "Order - cannot be changed once dispatched".

types.name: Hot Spot
types.description: A question, risk, problem or disagreement. Mark it and keep going; resolve it later.
types.whenToUse: Wherever something is unclear or contested - the more, the better.
types.writingRule: A question or a problem statement: "What if the restaurant is closed?".
examples: What if the restaurant is closed?

types.name: Opportunity
types.description: An idea for making things better - often the answer to a Hot Spot.
types.whenToUse: In the problems-and-opportunities phase, next to what it would improve.
types.writingRule: A proposal: "Show estimated delivery time on the menu".
examples: Show delivery time on the menu

types.name: Swimlane
types.description: A horizontal band that separates parallel flows - per actor, department or sub-process.
types.whenToUse: When the timeline has several things happening in parallel.

types.name: Boundary
types.description: A labelled area around the elements that belong to one candidate bounded context.
types.whenToUse: When a cluster of events clearly belongs together and speaks its own language.
